html:
DeDoDe v2 (Chalmers, Linköping University; 3DV 2024): sparse keypoints from a detector network, descriptions from a separate one (VGG19, plus DINOv2 for -G), dual-softmax matches as keypoint index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). MIT; DINOv2 Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: DeDoDe v2: Analyzing and Improving the DeDoDe Keypoint Detector, CVPR Workshops 2024, 2024-04-13
  • Original code: https://github.com/Parskatt/DeDoDe at 6d156183f4dc
  • Code licence: MIT (permissive); files: LICENSE, LICENSE-DINOv2
  • Weights licence: MIT
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/Parskatt/DeDoDe/blob/6d156183f4dc84cd704ae779eebc8350995c5b06/README.md#license ; https://github.com/Parskatt/DeDoDe/blob/6d156183f4dc84cd704ae779eebc8350995c5b06/LICENSE
  • Training data: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth) (Detector v2 and descriptors: MegaDepth (README training section, papers); DINOv2 (-G, frozen): LVD-142M (Meta).)
  • Options: size = 784 (>= 56), max_keypoints = 10000 (>= 1)
  • Kernel libraries: none (not implemented yet)
  • Variants: dedode-v2-b, dedode-v2-g
  • Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): dedode-v2-b 3000x4000 (1.9 GiB peak allocated, 3.8 reserved); dedode-v2-g 3000x4000 (2.5 GiB peak allocated, 4.5 reserved)
  • dedode-v2-b 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 50 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • dedode-v2-b original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream DeDoDe-L v2 + descriptor B, 10000 keypoints
  • dedode-v2-g original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream DeDoDe-L v2 + descriptor G, 10000 keypoints
  • dedode-v2-b load / first call: original 3.73 s / 1.099 s, portable 0.67 s / 0.753 s
  • dedode-v2-g load / first call: original 6.36 s / 1.509 s, portable 1.12 s / 1.038 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.011 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.002 and p99 <= 0.001 (absolute error of the output keypoints1).

Limitations

  • Sparse output: no dense warp. result.matches() gives the matched points for estimate_pose; pairs are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
  • One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
  • No exportable module: the match counts are data-dependent (torch.compile runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
  • Images are resized to a size x size square (default 784, as upstream) whatever their aspect ratio; the dual softmax holds a max_keypoints^2 matrix (10000 keypoints: 400 MB per float32 copy).
  • Upright only: the released descriptors are not trained for in-plane rotations.
